stories.headline: Google expands Lyria 3 Pro into mainstream workflow surfaces
stories.summary: Google said Lyria 3 Pro can generate tracks up to three minutes long with stronger song-structure control, and is rolling it into Gemini, Google Vids, Vertex AI, AI Studio, and ProducerAI. That is a distribution signal, not just a model-improvement signal.

stories.headline: Suno still looks like the biggest paid-scale signal in AI music
stories.summary: Music Business Worldwide reported Suno CEO Mikey Shulman said Suno reached 2 million paid subscribers, $300 million ARR, and 100 million users. Treat it as a company claim, but it remains strategically relevant because it suggests the category has real willingness to pay.

stories.headline: IFPI says recorded music reached $31.7B in 2025 and 837M paid subscriptions
stories.summary: Recorded music remains structurally large and growing. That means the opportunity is real, but it also increases pressure to find a defensible niche within a very noisy stack.

stories.headline: U.S. legal posture still leaves AI-training copyright questions unresolved
stories.summary: Music Ally reported the White House said courts should resolve whether training on copyrighted material is fair use, while Reuters' legal review said 2025 cases increasingly turn on lawful sourcing, piracy risk, and market-harm analysis. The takeaway is not certainty; it is continued legal ambiguity with strong importance on data provenance.

stories.headline: Moises/Water & Music survey still supports workflow-first adoption
stories.summary: Among 1,525 surveyed musicians, pros used AI more than hobbyists, but the biggest use case was still stem separation at 71%, versus 24% for full-song generation. Trust and rights concerns remained high.

stories.headline: Deezer is commercializing AI-detection infrastructure as fraud pressure rises
stories.summary: Reuters reported Deezer licensed its AI-detection tool to Sacem, said it removed up to 85% of fraudulent AI streams from its royalty pool in 2025, and said it now receives around 60,000 fully AI-created tracks per day. That is a strong signal that trust/compliance tooling is becoming part of the music stack.

stories.headline: UNESCO warns creator economics remain under pressure
stories.summary: UNESCO projected up to 24% revenue losses for music creators by 2028 from generative AI outputs and highlighted market concentration plus opaque curation systems as structural risks.

themes.workflow_over_hype: The strongest evidence still favors AI tools that remove friction inside existing music workflows rather than tools that fully replace musicians.
themes.rights_cleanliness_matters_more: The legal and commercial environment continues to reward clean sourcing, transparency, and rights clarity.
themes.scale_is_real_but_not_enough: Suno's scale signal and Google's distribution show the category is real, but they also make undifferentiated AI music apps less defensible.
themes.trust_infrastructure_is_rising: Fraud, spam, and impersonation are turning trust and detection into real product categories inside music tech.
themes.musio_implication: Musio should keep leaning toward trustworthy creator infrastructure: realistic musical output, human control, workflow fit, and commercially usable results.
